title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' Grothendieck sets up the topological, discrete-group counterpart of decomposition and inertia groups at a point x of a surface. To do this he needs the fundamental group of a punctured germ of neighbourhood D*_x, and the previous page starts a digression on coverings of an abstract germ of space S = (S, 𝓛).

Set-up. A germ of space is a space S together with a filtering family 𝓛 of 'neighbourhoods' S_i, i.e. essentially a pro-object (S_i). A covering of the germ is a covering S'_i → S_i of some member of the family, taken up to restriction. Rev(S) is the filtered 2-colimit of the categories Rev(S_i).

(54) The functor Rev(S) → (Germs)/S sends a covering to the germ (S'_i, inverse image of 𝓛). It is fully faithful. The germs over S lying in its essential image are called étale coverings of S. So Rev(S) is equivalent to the full subcategory of germs over S formed by étale coverings.

Universal coverings. Assume Rev(S) is 'multigaloisienne'. This means a (non-finite, discrete-π1) Galois-type category, not necessarily connected, equivalent to a disjoint sum of categories of G-sets. Then:
- Its 1-connected objects are called universal coverings.
- They form a groupoid, which is connected iff Rev(S) is Galois, i.e. iff the germ S is 0-connected.
- Each universal covering S~ is itself a 1-connected germ.
- One defines π1(S, S~), using S~ as a 'base point' in the style of SGA 1 pro-representable fibre functors.

(55) This gives the canonical isomorphism π1(S, S~) ≅ Aut_{Rev(S)}(S~). The margin stresses that this π1 is the π1 of the abstract Galois category Rev(S), 'computed' at the object S~.

Next page: this is applied to the punctured germ D*_x at a point where X is a surface. Rev(D*_x) is an ordinary Galois category with π1 ≅ T_x, the orientation module (≅ Z). Its universal coverings form a connected groupoid with fundamental group T_x. This is the topological model of an inertia group ≅ Ẑ(1) in the arithmetic setting.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statements are standard, given the definitions.
Existence of universal coverings needs the 'multigaloisienne' hypothesis, which he explicitly assumes. Local connectedness conditions on the members of 𝓛 are implicit.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine set-up of Galois-category formalism for germs of topological spaces, preparatory to defining discrete inertia at punctures. It is standard and well within known frameworks.
transcription_corrections: On the previous page, 'groupe d'inertie[?]' should almost certainly read 'germe d'espace(s)', i.e. (S, 𝓛) is a germ of space. 'groupe résiduel ... D*_{x,π}' is likely 'germe résiduel/épointé'.
Line 3: 'S' au-dessus de S' — the germ S'; reading confirmed.
'Supposons [-maintenant-]': the struck word looks like 'qu'en outre' or similar; minor.
'(S S)' under π1 at the bottom is the reference label '(55)'.
